BOOK ONE · LESSON 133

Sensational news! 爆炸性新闻！

爆炸性新闻！

A dialogue lesson in which a reporter interviews the film star Karen Marsh, who says she has just made a new film but is going to retire because she feels very tired. Kate and Liz then read about the news in a newspaper, and the reporter's account is reported in indirect (reported) speech. The story introduces the structures for reported speech: 'Let's ...', 'She told me she had just made a new film' (tense backshift), and 'I wonder why!'. The workbook drills comprehension of the dialogue and the newspaper article, and choosing between 'told' and 'said'; the grammar workbook changes direct speech into indirect speech.

New words & expressions 生词和短语

reporter /rɪ'pɔːtə/
n. 记者
sensational /sen'seɪʃənəl/
adj. 爆炸性的，耸人听闻的
mink coat /mɪŋk kəʊt/
n. 貂皮大衣

Notes on the text 课文注释

1. Let's = Let us.

常用于第一人称的祈使句中，用来表示请求、建议、命令。

2. She told me she had just made a new film.

这是间接引语的又一个例子，这句话中含有一个用过去时引述动词的结构。如果我们对一下马什小姐对记者说的话（直接引语）和报上刊载的记者的复述（间接引语），就不难发现，间接引语的动词时态往往要倒移。而这种倒移的普遍规则是：现在时变成过去时，现在完成时变成过去完成时。

3. I wonder why!

我很想知道为什么。
